title: What are the strange marks on Ruhee's old page?
description: A loose, yellowed page slips out of an old book and lands on the floor, covered in strange marks. Ruhee's father says the marks are numbers written four thousand years ago, and the video stops on how those people would write twenty, fifty or one hundred.
teaching_notes: One idea: numbers have not always been written the way we write them, and each way had to be invented. Collect guesses about twenty, fifty and one hundred and confirm none, because the chapter answers it. Watch for students who think the old marks were pictures and not numbers.

source: A loose page of strange symbols
video_script.why: Before any system is taught, the child meets the puzzle that drives the chapter: our digits were invented, and older people wrote numbers in other ways.
video_script.substitution: Picture a page of marks that look like drawings, yet stand for numbers.
video_script.anchor: Ruhee and Ruhee's father with the old book and the loose page that slipped out of it

names.Ruhee: the curious girl who finds the page of old number symbols

hold_back: how the old marks stand for numbers
never_show: any digit or numeral on screen
maths_rules: The marks on the page are drawn as small wedge and pebble shapes with no readable value; none is decoded.
The father says the marks are numbers written about four thousand years ago, by the people of Mesopotamia.
The open question is how those people would have written twenty, fifty or one hundred; it is never answered.
No digits or symbols are drawn on screen at any time.
video_script.design: One idea: number writing was invented, and there were other ways. Assumes nothing. The page stays to the end and the question is left open.
